diagnostics.message:
[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run1]
google_alloydb_user.users is provisioned on google_alloydb_cluster.primary without any ordering guarantee relative to google_alloydb_instance.primary. Per the provider documentation, database users should only be created after the primary instance exists (the official examples attach depends_on = [google_alloydb_instance.default] to google_alloydb_user), since user provisioning requires the instance backing the cluster to be in place. Add a bare `depends_on = [google_alloydb_instance.primary]` to google_alloydb_user.users.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run2]
`google_alloydb_user.users` only depends on `google_alloydb_cluster.primary` (via its `cluster` attribute). Creating database users is a real-world operation that requires the cluster's primary instance to exist first — the official provider documentation for google_alloydb_user includes `depends_on = [google_alloydb_instance...]` in every example. Without this ordering, Terraform may create the users concurrently with (or before) `google_alloydb_instance.primary`, and user creation can fail or race against instance provisioning. Add an explicit `depends_on = [google_alloydb_instance.primary]`; there is no attribute on the user resource that can reference the instance, so a data-dependency fix is not applicable.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run3]
google_alloydb_user.users only depends on google_alloydb_cluster.primary (via the cluster attribute), but creating database users in an AlloyDB cluster requires the cluster's primary instance to exist and be ready first. The provider documentation's own google_alloydb_user examples include depends_on = [google_alloydb_instance.default] for this reason. Without this ordering, user creation can race ahead of instance provisioning and fail.
